[LLM] WordPress backdoor authentication via tEcaKKXEsb cookie or new_code POST parameter Installation High
Detects inbound HTTP POST requests containing the campaign-specific authentication cookie 'tEcaKKXEsb' or the 'new_code' parameter the backdoor uses to ingest base64-encoded PHP. Both strings are unique to this GoDaddy-reported family and survive obfuscation rotation. Rationale: Two needle-in-haystack strings called out verbatim by GoDaddy and quoted in the article — 'tEcaKKXEsb' cookie and 'new_code' POST parameter — that have no benign reason to appear in inbound traffic. Any single hit is investigable. Defender/Falcon left empty because EDR doesn't reliably capture L7 request bodies/cookies; these only surface in web-tier / WAF telemetry. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/wordpress-malware-campaign-hides-payloads-in-steam-profiles/
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1071.001
Data sourcesWeb.Web
union isfuzzy=true
(AppServiceHTTPLogs
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where CsMethod =~ "POST"
  | where Cookie has "tEcaKKXEsb" or CsUriQuery has "new_code="
  | project TimeGenerated, Host=CsHost, ClientIP=CIp, Method=CsMethod, Uri=CsUriStem, Query=CsUriQuery, Cookie, UA=UserAgent, Status=ScStatus, Src="AppServiceHTTPLogs"),
(CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where RequestMethod =~ "POST"
  | where RequestCookies has "tEcaKKXEsb" or RequestURL has "new_code="
  | project TimeGenerated, Host=DestinationHostName, ClientIP=SourceIP, Method=RequestMethod, Uri=RequestURL, Query=RequestURL, Cookie=RequestCookies, UA=RequestClientApplication, Status=tostring(EventOutcome), Src="CommonSecurityLog"),
(W3CIISLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where csMethod =~ "POST"
  | where csUriQuery has "new_code=" or csUriStem has "new_code="
  | project TimeGenerated, Host=Computer, ClientIP=cIP, Method=csMethod, Uri=csUriStem, Query=csUriQuery, Cookie="<not-logged>", UA=csUserAgent, Status=tostring(scStatus), Src="W3CIISLog")
| order by TimeGenerated desc
@http.method:POST AND (@http.request.headers.cookie:*tEcaKKXEsb* OR @http.url:*new_code=* OR @http.url_details.queryString:*new_code=*)
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Web where Web.http_method=POST AND (Web.http_user_agent="*" AND (Web.cookie="*tEcaKKXEsb*" OR Web.uri_query="*new_code=*" OR Web.url="*new_code=*")) by Web.src Web.dest Web.url Web.http_user_agent
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Web where Web.http_method=POST AND (Web.http_user_agent="*" AND (Web.cookie="*tEcaKKXEsb*" OR Web.uri_query="*new_code=*" OR Web.url="*new_code=*")) by Web.src Web.dest Web.url Web.http_user_agent
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
[LLM] WordPress server / browser egress to hello-mywordl[.]info (stage-2 JS loader) Command & Control High
Alerts on any DNS/HTTP egress to hello-mywordl[.]info — the article's named stage-2 domain serving the injected JavaScript disguised as asahi-jquery-min-bundle / lodash.core.min.js. Catches both the WP server fetching the payload and end-user browsers loading the injected library on infected sites. Rationale: Single named domain IOC (hello-mywordl[.]info) called out verbatim by BleepingComputer / GoDaddy as the stage-2 loader URL. A multi-source union (DNS + L7 web + WAF) catches both the WP origin pulling the payload and end-user clients loading the injected JS. No legitimate use of this domain. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/wordpress-malware-campaign-hides-payloads-in-steam-profiles/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105 T1059.007
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Web.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
let BadDomain = dynamic(["hello-mywordl.info"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(DeviceNetworkEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where RemoteUrl has_any (BadDomain)
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Src="NetworkEvent"),
(DeviceEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where ActionType in ("DnsQueryResponse","InboundConnectionAccepted") and RemoteUrl has_any (BadDomain)
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName=AccountName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Src="DeviceEvent")
| order by Timestamp desc
let BadDomain = dynamic(["hello-mywordl.info"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(DnsEvents
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where Name has_any (BadDomain)
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Indicator=Name, Type="DNS", Src="DnsEvents"),
(ImDnsActivity
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DnsQuery has_any (BadDomain)
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, ClientIP=SrcIpAddr, Indicator=DnsQuery, Type="DNS", Src="ImDnsActivity"),
(ImWebSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where Url has_any (BadDomain) or HttpHostName has_any (BadDomain)
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, ClientIP=SrcIpAddr, Indicator=coalesce(Url,HttpHostName), Type="Web", Src="ImWebSession"),
(CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DestinationHostName has_any (BadDomain) or RequestURL has_any (BadDomain)
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DeviceName, ClientIP=SourceIP, Indicator=coalesce(RequestURL,DestinationHostName), Type="CEF", Src="CommonSecurityLog")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] PHP / web-runtime process spawning cURL with SSL verification disabled Command & Control Medium
Hunts for web-server processes (php-fpm, php-cgi, apache2, nginx, w3wp) invoking curl with -k / --insecure / CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER=false. The article explicitly names disabled SSL verification in cURL as a campaign tell — used to talk to Steam and to hello-mywordl[.]info without TLS pinning hassle. Rationale: The article explicitly lists 'disabled SSL verification in cURL requests' as an IOC. Pairing that flag with a web-runtime parent (php-fpm/apache/nginx/w3wp) is high-signal — sysadmins debugging with curl -k do so from interactive shells, not from PHP-FPM workers. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/wordpress-malware-campaign-hides-payloads-in-steam-profiles/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1573 T1505.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
let WebSvcParents = dynamic(["php-fpm","php","php-cgi","php.exe","php-cgi.exe","httpd","apache2","nginx","w3wp.exe"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (WebSvcParents)
| where FileName in~ ("curl","curl.exe","wget")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(\s-k\b|--insecure\b|--no-check-certificate\b|VERIFYPEER\s*=\s*(0|false))"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
let WebSvcParents = dynamic(["php-fpm","php","php-cgi","php.exe","php-cgi.exe","httpd","apache2","nginx","w3wp.exe"]);
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any (WebSvcParents) or ActingProcessName has_any (WebSvcParents)
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("curl","curl.exe","wget")
| where TargetProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(\s-k\b|--insecure\b|--no-check-certificate\b|VERIFYPEER\s*=\s*(0|false))"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: PHP / Web-Runtime Spawning cURL with SSL Verification Disabled
id: f3b8d2a4-1c6e-49a7-9b1f-2c8d4a6e7711
description: Web-server processes (php-fpm, apache2, nginx, w3wp) spawning curl with -k/--insecure — matches the GoDaddy-reported WordPress Steam-comment campaign which disables TLS verification when fetching its stage-2 loader.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/wordpress-malware-campaign-hides-payloads-in-steam-profiles/
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/01
tags:
  - attack.t1071.001
  - attack.t1573
  - attack.t1505.003
logsource:
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/php-fpm'
      - '/php-cgi'
      - '/php'
      - '\php.exe'
      - '\php-cgi.exe'
      - '/httpd'
      - '/apache2'
      - '/nginx'
      - '\w3wp.exe'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
      - '\curl.exe'
  selection_args:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - ' -k '
      - ' --insecure'
      - 'VERIFYPEER=0'
      - 'VERIFYPEER=false'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_args
level: medium
(source:linux.auditd @process.parent.name:(php-fpm OR php OR php-cgi OR apache2 OR httpd OR nginx) @process.name:curl @process.command_line:(*" -k "* OR *"--insecure"* OR *VERIFYPEER=0* OR *VERIFYPEER=false*)) OR (source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\php-cgi.exe OR *\php.exe OR *\w3wp.exe) @Image:(*\curl.exe OR *\CURL.EXE) @CommandLine:(*" -k "* OR *"--insecure"*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/curl(\.exe)?$/i
| ParentBaseFileName=/(php-fpm|php-cgi|php|httpd|apache2|nginx|w3wp\.exe)$/i
| regex("(?i)(\\s-k\\b|--insecure|VERIFYPEER\\s*=\\s*(0|false))", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("php-fpm","php","php-cgi","php.exe","php-cgi.exe","httpd","apache2","nginx","w3wp.exe") AND Processes.process_name IN ("curl","curl.exe") AND (Processes.process="* -k *" OR Processes.process="*--insecure*" OR Processes.process="*VERIFYPEER*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("php-fpm","php","php-cgi","php.exe","php-cgi.exe","httpd","apache2","nginx","w3wp.exe") AND Processes.process_name IN ("curl","curl.exe") AND (Processes.process="* -k *" OR Processes.process="*--insecure*" OR Processes.process="*VERIFYPEER*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("f86b0cd23c753f62d2b83d59270bcecb8403427aa19a89272d8b91251a740ea1") or SHA1 in~ ("f86b0cd23c753f62d2b83d59270bcecb8403427aa19a89272d8b91251a740ea1") or MD5 in~ ("f86b0cd23c753f62d2b83d59270bcecb8403427aa19a89272d8b91251a740ea1")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("f86b0cd23c753f62d2b83d59270bcecb8403427aa19a89272d8b91251a740ea1") or SHA1 in~ ("f86b0cd23c753f62d2b83d59270bcecb8403427aa19a89272d8b91251a740ea1") or MD5 in~ ("f86b0cd23c753f62d2b83d59270bcecb8403427aa19a89272d8b91251a740ea1")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["f86b0cd23c753f62d2b83d59270bcecb8403427aa19a89272d8b91251a740ea1"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] praisonai-platform: POST /workspaces/*/members with role=owner (CVE-2026-47413) Exploitation High
Hunts the CVE-2026-47413 primitive: a POST to /workspaces/{id}/members whose body contains role=owner, returning 201. The vulnerable endpoint accepts owner grants from any member-tier token, so any successful 201 on this path warrants review against the caller's known role. Rationale: Detection is grounded in the exact route the advisory names (`POST /workspaces/{workspace_id}/members` at workspaces.py:92-101) and the documented response status 201. No external corroboration beyond the GHSA advisory itself; the CVE is freshly published and there are no third-party write-ups yet. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8g2p-pqm3-fcfh
ATT&CKT1068 T1078.004
Data sourcesWeb.Web
// Defender Advanced Hunting does not natively ingest praisonai-platform HTTP logs.
// If the app is fronted by an MDA-monitored proxy that ships to CloudAppEvents, pivot there:
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in~ ("HttpRequest","ApiCall")
| where RawEventData has "/workspaces/" and RawEventData has "/members"
| where RawEventData has_any ("\"role\":\"owner\"","role=owner")
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, AccountObjectId, IPAddress, UserAgent, ObjectName, RawEventData
| order by Timestamp desc
// Path 1 — Azure App Service hosting praisonai-platform
let AppHits = AppServiceHTTPLogs
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where CsMethod =~ "POST"
    | where CsUriStem matches regex @"(?i)/workspaces/[^/]+/members/?$"
    | where ScStatus == 201
    | project TimeGenerated, CsHost, CsUriStem, CsUriQuery, CsUsername, CIp, UserAgent, ScStatus;
// Path 2 — generic ASIM web session table (covers WAF / reverse proxy / API gateway)
let WebHits = ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where HttpMethod =~ "POST"
    | where Url matches regex @"(?i)/workspaces/[^/]+/members/?$"
    | where HttpStatusCode in ("200","201")
    | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, Url, HttpMethod, HttpStatusCode, HttpRequestBodyBytes, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, DstHostname;
union isfuzzy=true AppHits, WebHits
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] praisonai-platform: identity-swap chain — owner grant followed by login from the granted account Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects the full CVE-2026-47413 exploit chain: a successful POST /workspaces/{id}/members with role=owner from caller A, followed within 1 hour by an authentication from a different identity (B) that begins acting on the same workspace from the same source IP. This is the 'second-identity owner' fingerprint the advisory describes. Rationale: Encodes the exploit chain steps 2-4 from the advisory: caller A grants user B owner via POST .../members (201), then within an hour user B authenticates from the same source IP. The same-IP + different-identity within a short window is the specific fingerprint the advisory calls out as hard to attribute via in-app audit logs alone. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8g2p-pqm3-fcfh
ATT&CKT1078 T1098 T1556
Data sourcesWeb.Web Authentication.Authentication
// Pivots on CloudAppEvents if the praisonai app is API-instrumented to MDA.
let GrantWindow = 1h;
let Grants = CloudAppEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(24h)
    | where RawEventData has "/workspaces/" and RawEventData has "/members"
    | where RawEventData has_any ("\"role\":\"owner\"","role=owner")
    | project GrantTime = Timestamp, GrantorIp = IPAddress, GrantorObjectId = AccountObjectId, GrantUrl = ObjectName, GrantRaw = RawEventData;
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(24h)
| where ActionType in~ ("Logon","LogIn","UserLoggedIn")
| join kind=inner Grants on $left.IPAddress == $right.GrantorIp
| where Timestamp between (GrantTime .. GrantTime + GrantWindow)
| where AccountObjectId != GrantorObjectId
| project GrantTime, LoginTime = Timestamp, DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, GrantTime), GrantorIp, GrantorObjectId, NewIdentity = AccountObjectId, NewIdentityName = AccountDisplayName, GrantUrl
| order by GrantTime desc
let GrantWindow = 1h;
let Grants = (union isfuzzy=true
    (AppServiceHTTPLogs
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
        | where CsMethod =~ "POST"
        | where CsUriStem matches regex @"(?i)/workspaces/[^/]+/members/?$"
        | where ScStatus == 201
        | project GrantTime = TimeGenerated, GrantorIp = CIp, GrantorUser = CsUsername, GrantUrl = CsUriStem),
    (ImWebSession
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
        | where HttpMethod =~ "POST"
        | where Url matches regex @"(?i)/workspaces/[^/]+/members/?$"
        | where HttpStatusCode in ("200","201")
        | project GrantTime = TimeGenerated, GrantorIp = SrcIpAddr, GrantorUser = SrcUsername, GrantUrl = Url));
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where ResultType == 0

[LLM] Vitest UI server launched with non-loopback --api.host / --host (CVE-2026-47429 exposure) Weaponization High
Hunts process creations where node/npm/yarn/pnpm spawns Vitest UI bound to a non-loopback interface via --api.host or --host. Pre-4.1.0 this implicitly grants remote callers file-read and RCE through the /__vitest_attachment__, saveTestFile and rerun APIs. Rationale: Article §Impact lists '--api.host' / api.host config as the precondition for the vulnerability. Pre-extracting the host arg and excluding loopback is the cleanest article-specific filter — every other use of node.exe with vitest is irrelevant. Cross-checked vendor advisory pages and the related GHSA-9crc-q9x8-hgqq (Vitest CSWSH) which confirms the same exposure model. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/security/advisories/GHSA-9crc-q9x8-hgqq • https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/security • https://vitest.dev/config/api.html
ATT&CKT1574 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","npx.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","npx.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "vitest"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--ui","--browser")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--api.host","--host","api.host")
| extend HostArg = extract(@"(?i)--(?:api\.)?host(?:[= ])(\S+)", 1, ProcessCommandLine)
| where isnotempty(HostArg) and HostArg !in~ ("127.0.0.1","localhost","::1")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, HostArg, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName has_any (@"\node.exe", @"\npm.exe", @"\yarn.exe", @"\pnpm.exe", @"\npx.exe")
| where CommandLine has "vitest"
| where CommandLine has_any ("--ui","--browser")
| where CommandLine has_any ("--api.host","--host","api.host")
| extend HostArg = extract(@"(?i)--(?:api\.)?host(?:[= ])(\S+)", 1, CommandLine)
| where isnotempty(HostArg) and HostArg !in~ ("127.0.0.1","localhost","::1")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, HostArg, ParentProcessName
title: Vitest UI Server Bound to Non-Loopback Interface (CVE-2026-47429)
id: 7b8c2f5e-1d4a-4f2c-9e3b-2a4c6d8e0f1a
description: Detects vitest UI / browser mode invoked with --api.host or --host pointing at a non-loopback interface, exposing the file-read and rerun-RCE APIs to the network.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5xrq-8626-4rwp
  - https://vitest.dev/config/api.html
author: detection-eng
date: 2026/06/01
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1574
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_img:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\node.exe'
      - '\npm.exe'
      - '\yarn.exe'
      - '\pnpm.exe'
      - '\npx.exe'
  selection_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains: 'vitest'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '--ui'
      - '--browser'
  selection_host:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '--api.host'
      - '--host'
      - 'api.host'
  filter_loopback:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '--host=127.0.0.1'
      - '--host 127.0.0.1'
      - '--host=localhost'
      - '--host localhost'
      - '--api.host=127.0.0.1'
      - '--api.host=localhost'
  condition: all of selection_* and not filter_loopback
level: high
source:(windows.security OR windows.sysmon) (@Image:(*\node.exe OR *\NODE.EXE OR *\npm.exe OR *\yarn.exe OR *\pnpm.exe OR *\npx.exe)) @CommandLine:(*vitest*) @CommandLine:(*--ui* OR *--browser*) @CommandLine:(*--api.host* OR *--host* OR *api.host*) -@CommandLine:(*localhost* OR *127.0.0.1* OR *::1*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/(node|npm|yarn|pnpm|npx)\.exe$/i
| CommandLine=/vitest/i
| CommandLine=/(--ui|--browser)/i
| CommandLine=/(--api\.host|--host|api\.host)/i
| NOT (CommandLine=/(127\.0\.0\.1|localhost|::1)/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

[LLM] Path-traversal exploit hitting Vitest /__vitest_attachment__ endpoint (CVE-2026-47429 PoC) Exploitation High
Hunts HTTP requests to the Vitest UI server's /__vitest__/ or /__vitest_attachment__ endpoints carrying the Windows-specific '\?\..\' path-traversal payload (or URL-encoded equivalents). This is the literal PoC URL from the advisory bypassing isFileServingAllowed. Rationale: PoC §3 in the advisory uses the literal URL '/__vitest_attachment__?path=...?\..\..\secret.txt'. The '?\..\' sequence is article-specific because the bypass relies on Windows-only quirk (Linux errors on '?' directory). URL-encoded variants %3F%5C..%5C are what curl/browsers send on wire. Cross-checked the vendor advisory and the related Vite CVE-2026-39363 confirming the dev-server-traversal family pattern. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5xrq-8626-4rwp • https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/security/advisories/GHSA-9crc-q9x8-hgqq • https://securityonline.info/vite-vulnerabilities-cve-2026-39364-arbitrary-file-read/
ATT&CKT1190 T1083 T1006
Data sourcesWeb.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemotePort == 51204 or LocalPort == 51204 or RemoteUrl has "__vitest"
| where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("__vitest_attachment__","__vitest__")
| where RemoteUrl matches regex @"(?i)(%3F%5C|%3F/|\?\\|\?/)\.\.[\\/]"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, LocalIP, LocalPort, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl
| order by Timestamp desc
// Primary: W3C IIS / reverse-proxy logs in front of the Vitest UI host
let TraversalRx = @"(?i)(%3F%5C|%3F/|\?\\|\?/)\.\.[\\/]";
(union isfuzzy=true
  (W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where csUriStem has_any ("__vitest_attachment__","__vitest__")
    | where strcat(csUriStem, "?", csUriQuery) matches regex TraversalRx
    | extend Url = strcat(csUriStem, "?", csUriQuery), SrcIp = cIP, DstHost = Computer, Method = csMethod, Status = scStatus, UserAgent = csUserAgent
    | project TimeGenerated, SrcIp, DstHost, sPort, Method, Url, Status, UserAgent, Source="W3CIISLog"),
  (CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where RequestURL has_any ("__vitest_attachment__","__vitest__")
    | where RequestURL matches regex TraversalRx
    | project TimeGenerated, SrcIp=SourceIP, DstHost=DestinationHostName, sPort=DestinationPort, Method=RequestMethod, Url=RequestURL, Status=tostring(EventOutcome), UserAgent=RequestClientApplication, Source="CommonSecurityLog"),
  (ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where Url has_any ("__vitest_attachment__","__vitest__")
    | where Url matches regex TraversalRx
    | project TimeGenerated, SrcIp=SrcIpAddr, DstHost=DstHostname, sPort=DstPortNumber, Method=HttpMethod, Url, Status=tostring(HttpStatusCode), UserAgent=HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, Source="ImWebSession"))
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Post-exploit shell spawned by Vitest node.exe via rerun / saveTestFile (CVE-2026-47429) Exploitation Medium
Hunts node.exe processes whose command line contains 'vitest' spawning interactive shells, script hosts, or LOLBins. This is the post-exploitation shape when an attacker uses the rerun API to execute attacker-controlled test files written via saveTestFile — equivalent to arbitrary code execution. Rationale: Article §Details: 'it's possible to run arbitrary script by writing a script as a test file using saveTestFile and running it using rerun. This means exposing the API / Vitest UI is equivalent to giving script execution access.' The execution surface is node.exe (the vitest runner) spawning whatever the attacker's malicious test file invokes. Pivoting on parent=node.exe + parent cmdline contains 'vitest' + non-test child binary is the cleanest article-grounded shape. Cross-checked vendor advisory. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5xrq-8626-4rwp • https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/security/advisories/GHSA-9crc-q9x8-hgqq
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1059.003 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "vitest"
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","net.exe","whoami.exe","hostname.exe","systeminfo.exe","nslookup.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
// Reduce FP: vitest legitimately launches node.exe worker children — only flag non-node children
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith @"\node.exe"
| where NewProcessName has_any (@"\cmd.exe",@"\powershell.exe",@"\pwsh.exe",@"\wscript.exe",@"\cscript.exe",@"\mshta.exe",@"\rundll32.exe",@"\regsvr32.exe",@"\bitsadmin.exe",@"\certutil.exe",@"\curl.exe",@"\wget.exe",@"\whoami.exe",@"\hostname.exe",@"\systeminfo.exe",@"\nslookup.exe")
| where Account !endswith "$"
// Join to a recent vitest invocation on the same host
| join kind=inner (
    SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where CommandLine has "vitest"
    | project VitestTime=TimeGenerated, Computer, VitestPid=NewProcessId, VitestCmd=CommandLine
  ) on Computer
| where TimeGenerated between (VitestTime .. VitestTime + 8h)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, VitestCmd

[LLM] Inbound TCP connection to Vitest UI port 51204 from non-loopback source Delivery Medium
Hunts inbound TCP connections to TCP/51204 (Vitest UI default) on endpoints from non-loopback peers — the observable signal that a misconfigured Vitest UI is being reached over the network. Pair with UC1 (the cmdline misconfiguration) for confirmation. Rationale: Article §PoC step 1 uses default 'http://localhost:51204/' — 51204 is Vitest UI's hard-coded default port. Any inbound to that port from non-loopback on a node.exe-driven listener is by definition the exposure path the advisory warns about. Cross-checked the vitest docs and the related GHSA-9crc-q9x8-hgqq advisory which references the same default port. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5xrq-8626-4rwp • https://vitest.dev/config/api.html • https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/security/advisories/GHSA-9crc-q9x8-hgqq
ATT&CKT1133 T1190
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where LocalPort == 51204 and Protocol == "Tcp"
| where ActionType in ("InboundConnectionAccepted","ConnectionSuccess","ListeningConnectionCreated")
| where RemoteIPType != "Loopback" and RemoteIP !in ("127.0.0.1","::1","")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe")
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), ConnCount=count(), RemoteIps=make_set(RemoteIP, 20)
          by DeviceName, LocalIP, LocalPort, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by FirstSeen desc
// Sentinel sees this via ASIM ImNetworkSession (or vendor-specific firewall in CommonSecurityLog)
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstPortNumber == 51204 and NetworkProtocol =~ "tcp"
| where DvcAction in~ ("Allow","Allowed","Accept","") or isempty(DvcAction)
| where SrcIpAddr !in ("127.0.0.1","::1")
| where not(ipv4_is_in_range(SrcIpAddr, "127.0.0.0/8"))
| summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated), Sessions=count(), DstHosts=make_set(DstHostname, 20)
          by SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, DstPortNumber
| order by FirstSeen desc
title: Inbound Connection to Vitest UI Default Port 51204 (CVE-2026-47429)
id: 4d6f8a1b-3c5e-4d7f-9b2a-6c8e1f3d5b7a
description: Inbound TCP connection accepted on port 51204 (Vitest UI default) from a non-loopback source — the network-side observable of CVE-2026-47429 exposure.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5xrq-8626-4rwp
author: detection-eng
date: 2026/06/01
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1133
  - attack.t1190
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Initiated: 'false'
    DestinationPort: 51204
    Protocol: 'tcp'
  filter_loopback:
    SourceIp:
      - '127.0.0.1'
      - '::1'
  condition: selection and not filter_loopback
level: medium
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @DestinationPort:51204 -@SourceIp:(127.0.0.1 OR ::1) -CIDR(@SourceIp, 127.0.0.0/8) @Image:(*\node.exe OR *\NODE.EXE)
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4
| LocalPort=51204
| ConnectionDirection=1
| NOT (RemoteAddressIP4=/^(127\.|::1)/)
| ContextImageFileName=/\\node\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, LocalAddressIP4, LocalPort, RemoteAddressIP4, ContextImageFileName], function=count())
# log group: /aws/vpc/flowlogs
fields @timestamp, srcAddr, dstAddr, dstPort, action, bytes
| filter dstPort = 51204 and action = "ACCEPT"
| filter not (srcAddr like /^127\./ or srcAddr = "::1")
| stats count(*) as sessions, sum(bytes) as bytes, earliest(@timestamp) as firstSeen by srcAddr, dstAddr
| sort firstSeen desc

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender · Microsoft Teams external-tenant chat from unverified IT-helpdesk impersonator
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft)
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]

Microsoft Teams external-tenant chat from unverified IT-helpdesk impersonator Delivery High
External Teams chat where displayName contains 'helpdesk' or 'IT support' — common 2024+ vishing pattern (Storm-1811, Black Basta, UNC6692). No CIM data model maps to Teams chats; uses raw O365 audit logs.
ATT&CKT1566.004 T1566
Data sourcesCloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application == "Microsoft Teams"
| where ActionType == "MessageSent"
| where RawEventData has "ExternalParticipants"
| extend SenderDisplayName = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).SenderDisplayName)
| where SenderDisplayName matches regex @"(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)"
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, IPAddress, ActivityType, SenderDisplayName, RawEventData
// External Teams chat — Teams audit lives in OfficeActivity.
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OfficeWorkload == "MicrosoftTeams"
| where Operation in~ ("MessageSent","ChatCreated","TeamsImpersonationDetected")
| where isnotempty(UserId)
| where Subject has_any ("IT","helpdesk","support","password","verify")
   or Recipients has_any ("IT","helpdesk")
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, Operation, Subject, Recipients,
          ClientIP, UserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc
CLOUD
`o365_management_activity`
  Workload=MicrosoftTeams Operation=MessageSent
  ExternalParticipants=*
| where match(SenderDisplayName, "(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)")
| stats count, earliest(_time) as firstTime, latest(_time) as lastTime
    by SenderUpn, SenderDisplayName, RecipientUpn, ChatId

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Privileged container launch — docker run --privileged from non-CI parent · [LLM] Container escape via cgroups release_agent write (CVE-2022-0492) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] runC binary modified outside package manager (CVE-2019-5736 / CVE-2024-21626) · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Containers on fire: from container escapes to supply chain attacks
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] TeamPCP Checkmarx KICS supply-chain stealer C2 callback (audit.checkmarx.cx / 94.154.172.43) · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Kubernetes API curl/wget with ServiceAccount token from container · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
[LLM] TeamPCP Checkmarx KICS supply-chain stealer C2 callback (audit.checkmarx.cx / 94.154.172.43) Command & Control High
Catches the post-compromise C2 beacon from the TeamPCP-poisoned KICS Docker image. Network egress to the hardcoded domain audit.checkmarx.cx or the IP 94.154.172.43 from any host running the tainted KICS scanner container. Rationale: Anchors on the exact IP 94.154.172.43 and FQDN audit.checkmarx.cx pre-extracted from the article — the TeamPCP-controlled C2 the KICS stealer talks to during scanning. High-fidelity because these are not generic infrastructure; only an org talking to Checkmarx KICS would even conceivably resolve audit.checkmarx.cx and that domain isn't on any legitimate Checkmarx documentation page (cross-check vs vendor).
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1195.002

let bad_ips = dynamic(["94.154.172.43"]);
let bad_domains = dynamic(["audit.checkmarx.cx"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in (bad_ips) or RemoteUrl has_any (bad_domains)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort, Protocol, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessSHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let bad_ips = dynamic(["94.154.172.43"]);
let bad_domains = dynamic(["audit.checkmarx.cx"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DstIpAddr in (bad_ips) or DstHostname has_any (bad_domains) or Url has_any (bad_domains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DstIpAddr, DstHostname, DstPortNumber, NetworkProtocol, Url

[LLM] Privileged container launch — docker run --privileged from non-CI parent Exploitation Medium
Detects docker / podman / nerdctl invocations carrying --privileged when the parent is not a known container runtime or CI runner. Privileged containers disable nearly all isolation primitives (all capabilities granted, full /dev access, no seccomp) and are the most common pre-condition for container escape in the article. Rationale: Anchors on the exact `--privileged` flag and `docker exec` strings quoted as code blocks in the article. The CI-parent exclusion catches the legitimate use cases (buildkitd, gitlab/jenkins/github runners) and keeps the alert focused on interactive-shell or unexpected-parent invocations, which is where supply-chain compromise or insider misuse shows up.
ATT&CKT1611 T1610
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("docker","podman","nerdctl")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "--privileged"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (" run "," create "," exec ")
| where not(InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("containerd-shim","buildkitd","kubelet","Runner.Listener","gitlab-runner","jenkins","github-runner"))
| where not(InitiatingProcessAccountName in~ ("jenkins","gitlab-runner","github-runner","buildkite-agent"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName in~ ("docker","podman","nerdctl") or ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\b(docker|podman|nerdctl)\b"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "--privileged"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (" run "," create "," exec ")
| where not(ParentProcessName has_any ("containerd-shim","buildkitd","kubelet","Runner.Listener","gitlab-runner","jenkins","github-runner"))
| where not(ActorUsername in~ ("jenkins","gitlab-runner","github-runner","buildkite-agent"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Privileged Container Launch via docker/podman --privileged
id: 9d7e1b22-3f64-4e8a-b1c0-5a2f8d4e9c33
description: docker / podman / nerdctl invoked with --privileged plus run|create|exec, indicating a fully privileged container that disables Linux isolation primitives and enables container-escape primitives discussed in the Kaspersky container attack-vectors article.
references:
    - https://securelist.com/container-attack-vectors/120010/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/01
tags:
    - attack.privilege_escalation
    - attack.t1611
    - attack.execution
    - attack.t1610
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: linux
detection:
    selection_bin:
        Image|endswith:
            - '/docker'
            - '/podman'
            - '/nerdctl'
    selection_flag:
        CommandLine|contains: '--privileged'
    selection_verb:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - ' run '
            - ' create '
            - ' exec '
    filter_parent:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - 'containerd-shim'
            - 'buildkitd'
            - 'kubelet'
            - 'gitlab-runner'
            - 'jenkins'
            - 'github-runner'
    condition: selection_bin and selection_flag and selection_verb and not filter_parent
falsepositives:
    - Hand-debugging by sysadmins (treat as a sensitive event regardless)
    - Legacy build pipelines that genuinely require --privileged (should be allow-listed by hostname/user)
level: medium

source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE (@process.executable.path:(*/docker OR */podman OR */nerdctl)) @process.command_line:*--privileged* @process.command_line:(*" run "* OR *" create "* OR *" exec "*) -@process.parent.executable.path:(*/containerd-shim* OR */buildkitd OR */kubelet OR */gitlab-runner OR */jenkins) -@user.name:(jenkins OR gitlab-runner OR github-runner)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\/(docker|podman|nerdctl)$/i CommandLine=/--privileged/i CommandLine=/\s(run|create|exec)\s/i
| NOT (ParentBaseFileName=/^(containerd-shim.*|buildkitd|kubelet|Runner\.Listener|gitlab-runner|jenkins|github-runner)$/i)
| NOT (UserName=/^(jenkins|gitlab-runner|github-runner|buildkite-agent)$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT

[LLM] Container escape via cgroups release_agent write (CVE-2022-0492) Exploitation High
Detects file writes to a release_agent path under /sys/fs/cgroup — the exact primitive abused by CVE-2022-0492 to escape a container and execute arbitrary commands on the host. Pairs the write with the canonical follow-up notify_on_release setting. Rationale: CVE-2022-0492 is explicitly called out in the article as a container-escape vulnerability whose root cause is improper privilege validation on the cgroups release_agent mechanism. The detection anchors on the exact filesystem object the exploit primitive must write to (release_agent + notify_on_release toggle) — there is no benign reason for a containerised workload to touch these files at runtime. Cross-checked against: • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2022-0492
ATT&CKT1611 T1068
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FolderPath has "/cgroup/" and (FileName == "release_agent" or FolderPath has "release_agent" or FileName == "notify_on_release")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in~ ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFilePath has "/cgroup/" and (TargetFileName == "release_agent" or TargetFilePath has "release_agent" or TargetFileName == "notify_on_release")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Container Escape via cgroups release_agent Write (CVE-2022-0492)

[LLM] runC binary modified outside package manager (CVE-2019-5736 / CVE-2024-21626) Installation High
Detects writes to the runC binary on disk by anything other than the legitimate package-manager toolchain. The article calls out CVE-2019-5736 (runC binary overwrite from a compromised container via /proc/self/exe) and CVE-2024-21626 (runC fd handling for host fs access) — both leave the runC executable modified on the node. Rationale: Anchors on the exact runC binary paths and the package-manager exclusion list — CVE-2019-5736 is unique in that successful exploitation requires writing to the host's runC executable from a container context, so any modification of /usr/bin/runc outside the dpkg/yum/snap toolchain is overwhelmingly indicative of either supply-chain compromise or active runC exploit. Also catches the post-exploit cleanup phase of CVE-2024-21626. Cross-checked against: • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2019-5736 • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2024-21626
ATT&CKT1611 T1554
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FolderPath in~ ("/usr/bin/runc","/usr/sbin/runc","/usr/local/bin/runc","/usr/bin/docker-runc","/usr/libexec/docker/docker-runc") or FileName in~ ("runc","docker-runc")
| where FolderPath has_any ("/usr/bin","/usr/sbin","/usr/local/bin","/usr/libexec")
| where not(InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("dpkg","apt","apt-get","yum","dnf","rpm","snap","snapd","zypper","containerd"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, ActionType, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in~ ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFilePath in~ ("/usr/bin/runc","/usr/sbin/runc","/usr/local/bin/runc","/usr/bin/docker-runc","/usr/libexec/docker/docker-runc")
| where not(ActingProcessName in~ ("dpkg","apt","apt-get","yum","dnf","rpm","snap","snapd","zypper","containerd"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256, EventType, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

description: Write to the runC executable on disk (/usr/bin/runc, /usr/sbin/runc, /usr/local/bin/runc, docker-runc variants) by a process that is not a known package manager. [LLM] Kubernetes API curl/wget with ServiceAccount token from container Actions on Objectives High
Detects the article's literal curl POST pattern against the Kubernetes API (`curl -k -X POST https://<kubernetes-url>/api/v1/namespaces/...`) and the canonical ServiceAccount token path. This is exactly the post-compromise behaviour described for the in-container malicious-actions vector — using the mounted /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token to talk to the cluster API. Rationale: Anchors directly on the article's verbatim Table 2 code block (`curl -k -X POST https://<kubernetes-url>/api/v1/namespaces/default/pods -H ...`) plus the canonical SA-token path the article explicitly calls out as automatically mounted and attacker-valuable. curl/wget shouldn't be hitting the API server in healthy pods — legitimate workloads use SDKs / kubectl.
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1528 T1613
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("curl","wget","http","httpie")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/api/v1/namespaces","/api/v1/pods","/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token","kubernetes.default.svc",":6443/api/",":8443/api/v1/")
| where not(InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("kubelet","kubectl","helm","argocd","flux"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName in~ ("curl","wget","http","httpie")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("/api/v1/namespaces","/api/v1/pods","/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token","kubernetes.default.svc",":6443/api/",":8443/api/v1/")
| where not(ParentProcessName in~ ("kubelet","kubectl","helm","argocd","flux"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Kubernetes API curl/wget with ServiceAccount Token Path from Container
id: 1f9b0d4e-8a37-4c25-b6e9-3d1a5e7f2c48
description: curl / wget / httpie referencing the Kubernetes API server (/api/v1/namespaces, /api/v1/pods, kubernetes.default.svc, :6443/api) or the canonical ServiceAccount token path. The article quotes verbatim `curl -k -X POST https://<kubernetes-url>/api/v1/namespaces/default/pods -H "..."` as the in-container abuse pattern.
references:
    - https://securelist.com/container-attack-vectors/120010/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/01
tags:
    - attack.credential_access
    - attack.t1552.001
    - attack.t1528

logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: linux
detection:
    selection_bin:
        Image|endswith:
            - '/curl'
            - '/wget'
            - '/http'
            - '/httpie'
    selection_kube:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/api/v1/namespaces'
            - '/api/v1/pods'
            - '/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token'
            - 'kubernetes.default.svc'
            - ':6443/api/'
            - ':8443/api/v1/'
    filter_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '/kubelet'
            - '/kubectl'
            - '/helm'
            - '/argocd'
            - '/flux'
    condition: selection_bin and selection_kube and not filter_parent
falsepositives:
    - In-cluster operators that legitimately curl the API server with their SA token (Prometheus k8s-sd, custom controllers) — allow-list by image/namespace
    - Init containers that probe the API server during pod start-up
level: high

source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.executable.path:(*/curl OR */wget OR */http OR */httpie) @process.command_line:(*"/api/v1/namespaces"* OR *"/api/v1/pods"* OR *"/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token"* OR *"kubernetes.default.svc"* OR *":6443/api/"*) -@process.parent.executable.path:(*/kubelet OR */kubectl OR */helm OR */argocd OR */flux)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\/(curl|wget|http|httpie)$/i CommandLine=/(\/api\/v1\/(namespaces|pods)|\/var\/run\/secrets\/kubernetes\.io\/serviceaccount\/token|kubernetes\.default\.svc|:6443\/api\/|:8443\/api\/v1\/)/i
| NOT ParentBaseFileName=/^(kubelet|kubectl|helm|argocd|flux)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
# log group: /aws/eks/<cluster-name>/cluster
fields @timestamp, user.username, sourceIPs, verb, requestURI, userAgent, objectRef.resource, objectRef.namespace, responseStatus.code
| filter userAgent like /^(curl|Wget|HTTPie)/i
      and user.username like /system:serviceaccount:/
      and verb in ["create","get","list","patch","delete","watch"]
| sort @timestamp desc

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2019-5736", "CVE-2022-0492", "CVE-2024-21626")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId

| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

title: Remote-Management (RMM) Tool Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0c
status: experimental
description: |
    AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera / Splashtop /
    RustDesk — RMM tools attackers commonly install for hands-on-
    keyboard access. Filter against the IT estate's known tool.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1219/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1219
    - attack.command-and-control
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\AnyDesk.exe'
            - '\TeamViewer.exe'
            - '\TeamViewer_Service.exe'
            - '\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe'
            - '\ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe'
            - '\atera_agent.exe'
            - '\SplashtopStreamer.exe'
            - '\RustDesk.exe'
            - '\NinjaOne.exe'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - IT-approved RMM in use across the estate. Maintain a known-IT-
      tool exclusion list per environment.
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe","kaseya*.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe","kaseya*.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("94.154.172.43") or RemoteUrl has_any ("audit.checkmarx.cx")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic(["94.154.172.43"]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["audit.checkmarx.cx"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)

   or Url has_any (BadDomains)

| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("24680027afadea90c7c713821e214b15cb6c922e67ac01109fb1edb3ee4741d9", "2a6a35f06118ff7d61bfd36a5788557b695095e7c9a609b4a01956883f146f50", "2b12cc5cc91ec483048abcbd6d523cdc9ebae3f3", "250f3633529457477a9f8fd3db3472e94383606a", "d47de3772f2d61a043e7047431ef4cf4", "e1023db24a29ab0229d99764e2c8deba") or SHA1 in~ ("24680027afadea90c7c713821e214b15cb6c922e67ac01109fb1edb3ee4741d9", "2a6a35f06118ff7d61bfd36a5788557b695095e7c9a609b4a01956883f146f50", "2b12cc5cc91ec483048abcbd6d523cdc9ebae3f3", "250f3633529457477a9f8fd3db3472e94383606a", "d47de3772f2d61a043e7047431ef4cf4", "e1023db24a29ab0229d99764e2c8deba") or MD5 in~ ("24680027afadea90c7c713821e214b15cb6c922e67ac01109fb1edb3ee4741d9", "2a6a35f06118ff7d61bfd36a5788557b695095e7c9a609b4a01956883f146f50", "2b12cc5cc91ec483048abcbd6d523cdc9ebae3f3", "250f3633529457477a9f8fd3db3472e94383606a", "d47de3772f2d61a043e7047431ef4cf4", "e1023db24a29ab0229d99764e2c8deba")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("24680027afadea90c7c713821e214b15cb6c922e67ac01109fb1edb3ee4741d9", "2a6a35f06118ff7d61bfd36a5788557b695095e7c9a609b4a01956883f146f50", "2b12cc5cc91ec483048abcbd6d523cdc9ebae3f3", "250f3633529457477a9f8fd3db3472e94383606a", "d47de3772f2d61a043e7047431ef4cf4", "e1023db24a29ab0229d99764e2c8deba") or SHA1 in~ ("24680027afadea90c7c713821e214b15cb6c922e67ac01109fb1edb3ee4741d9", "2a6a35f06118ff7d61bfd36a5788557b695095e7c9a609b4a01956883f146f50", "2b12cc5cc91ec483048abcbd6d523cdc9ebae3f3", "250f3633529457477a9f8fd3db3472e94383606a", "d47de3772f2d61a043e7047431ef4cf4", "e1023db24a29ab0229d99764e2c8deba") or MD5 in~ ("24680027afadea90c7c713821e214b15cb6c922e67ac01109fb1edb3ee4741d9", "2a6a35f06118ff7d61bfd36a5788557b695095e7c9a609b4a01956883f146f50", "2b12cc5cc91ec483048abcbd6d523cdc9ebae3f3", "250f3633529457477a9f8fd3db3472e94383606a", "d47de3772f2d61a043e7047431ef4cf4", "e1023db24a29ab0229d99764e2c8deba")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["24680027afadea90c7c713821e214b15cb6c922e67ac01109fb1edb3ee4741d9", "2a6a35f06118ff7d61bfd36a5788557b695095e7c9a609b4a01956883f146f50", "2b12cc5cc91ec483048abcbd6d523cdc9ebae3f3", "250f3633529457477a9f8fd3db3472e94383606a", "d47de3772f2d61a043e7047431ef4cf4", "e1023db24a29ab0229d99764e2c8deba"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc
